content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (especially 1-3 days ahead) when sentiment is positive or neutral, and underestimates when sentiment is negative or volatile.
- When sentiment turns positive sharply, model tends to overshoot and then correct — apply a downward adjustment in the 2nd-3rd day of the forecast horizon.
- In the presence of strong upward sentiment (e.g., >0.30), model often fails to capture the full magnitude of the rally — increase forecast by 10-15% of the recent 7-day average if sentiment >0.25.
- When sentiment is negative and prices are trending down, model underestimates the depth of the drop — add a 5-10% buffer below the forecast if sentiment < -0.30.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects after sharp spikes; if price rises >10% from 7-day average, reduce forecast by 5-8% in the next 3 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate the final 5-7 days — add 2-5% to the last 5 days if sentiment is positive or stable.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.20 or more in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast horizon smoothing — use 14-day rolling average instead of 30-day for correction.
